translations.text: All wisdom comes from the Lord, and it is with him forever.
If you desire wisdom, [?] the commandment, and the Lord will give it to you.
As you become greater, humble yourselves, so that you may find a [?].
For the Lord's power is great, and he is glorified through the humble.
Do not seek things that are difficult for you, and do not investigate things that are too hard.
Wisdom has exalted her children, and she welcomes those who seek her.
Do not be quick to speak while being sluggish and careless in your actions.
Do not put your trust in wealth gained unjustly, for it will not benefit you at all on the day of distress.
Stand among the elders and attach yourself to the wise person among them.
Do not trade your friend for the sake of a bargain, or a good brother for gold from Ophir.
Do you have daughters? Pay attention to their bodies, and do not [?] your face toward them.
Do not laugh with an ignorant person, lest your parents be insulted.
To the best of your ability, pay attention to yourself and your neighbor, and seek advice from wise people.
Authority over the earth is in the Lord's hand, and at the right time he raises up a suitable person over it.
A person's success is in the Lord's hand, and he bestows his glory on a scribe.
Do not be angry with your neighbor over any wrongdoing, and do not do anything arrogantly.
Good things and evil, life and death, poverty and wealth come from the Lord.
Do not call anyone blessed before he dies, and a person is known through his children.
He will stay with you for an hour, but if you stumble, he will not stay.
If a rich person falters, his friends support him; but if a poor person falls, his friends abandon him.
My son, provide for yourself according to what you have, and promptly offer a sacrifice to the Lord.
And she will give him the water of wisdom to drink; she will feed him the bread of understanding.
She will exalt him above his neighbors, and she will open his mouth in the midst of an assembly.
The Lord hates every abomination, and those who fear him do not love them.
They numbered six hundred thousand, those who had gathered in their stubbornness.
A wise person makes himself loved through his words, but the favors of fools will be wasted.
There is someone who does not sin because of his poverty.
A fool’s inner being is like a broken vessel: it cannot hold any knowledge.

If you open your mouth against your friend, do not be afraid, for reconciliation with him is possible—except when you insult him, act arrogantly toward him, reveal his secret, or strike him treacherously. Every friend will abandon you because of these things.
Listen, my children, to instruction about the mouth. Whoever guards it will not be ruined.
A person accustomed to insulting words will not learn discipline all his days.
All this is the book of the covenant of God Most High, the law that Moses entrusted to us as an inheritance for the congregations of Jacob.
Any suffering is better than suffering caused by those who hate, and any vengeance is better than an enemy’s vengeance.
I would rather live with a lion and a dragon than live with a woman who is wicked and quick to anger.
A woman who supports her husband is anger, blindness, and shame.
My heart was afraid of three things, and at the fourth my face fell: slander in a city, the gathering of a crowd, and a false accusation. All these are worse than death.
Like the sun rising in the Lord’s heights, so is a good woman in the orderly arrangement of her house.
Evils will come upon the one who does evil, and he will not know where they came from.
Whoever trusts it will find no rest and will not live in peace.
Many have held back, not because of wickedness; they were afraid of being cheated for nothing.
It is a miserable life to move from house to house, and he will not be able to open his mouth where he is staying.
“Come, stranger, prepare a table and feed me with what you have.”
When his father dies, he will be like someone who has not died, because he has left behind someone like himself.
Remain above them in all your dealings. Do not stain your honor.
If you mistreat him, he will get up and run away. And along what road will you search for him?
He lifts up their souls and gives light to their eyes, giving them healing, life, and blessing.
The life of the poor person is the bread he needs. Whoever deprives him of it is a murderer.
And do not trust in a sacrifice obtained through injustice, for the Lord is a judge, and human prestige counts for nothing before him.
Just as you showed yourself holy among us before them, so may you show your greatness among them before us.
If a well-taught man is properly satisfied, he does not gasp on his bed.
No evil will befall the one who fears the Lord; instead, he will find deliverance in his trial.
And he looks in this way at all the works of the Most High: two by two, one opposite another.
It eats every kind of food, but some food is better than other food.
A friend takes pleasure in his friend's happiness, but in a time of distress he will turn against him.
Sorrow dwells amid hardships, and the poor man's life is in his heart.
Listen to me, my holy children, and blossom like a rose planted beside running water.
A man who looks to a table that is not his own has no life. He will defile his soul with food that is not his, but a wise and educated man will guard himself against this.
Begging will be sweet in the mouth of the shameless person, but a fire will blaze within him.
Concerning the law of the Most High and the covenant, and a judgment that favors the ungodly.
A man's wickedness is better than a woman who does good, and a woman who brings shame will become a stumbling block.
And the moon, [?] in every activity of its appointed time, is the indicator of its seasons and an everlasting sign.
Their descendants stood firm in the covenants.

The blessing of every person and the covenant rested on Jacob's head. He acknowledged him with his blessings and gave him an inheritance. He determined his portions and divided them among twelve tribes.
And he showed mercy in the days of Moses. He and Caleb son of Jephunneh stood against them to keep the people from sin and to put an end to their wicked grumbling.
And before he rested forever, he testified before the Lord and the king: "I have taken no money [?] from anyone, not even a sandal." And no one accused him.
And he prophesied after his death. He told the king of his death and raised his voice from the earth in a prophecy, wiping out the people's lawlessness.
He was the one who brought famine upon them and humbled them in his zeal.
Then he came down and raised his hands over the whole assembly of the children of [?], to give the Lord's blessing from their lips and to glory in his name.
I will praise you, Lord, my king. I will bless you, God, my Savior. I will praise your name.

For you became my helper and protector, and you saved my body from destruction, from fabricated slander by a tongue and from the lips of those who practice falsehood, and in the presence of those who stood against me.
And from the fury of a flame around me—I was not burned—from the midst of a fire.
I blossomed like a vine that had spread out. My heart rejoiced in her. My foot stood on the straight path; I sought her from my youth.
I opened my mouth and spoke: "Acquire it for yourselves free of charge."
